I'll write some thoughts down on this briefly.  Firstly @fejau_inc is a smart guy and isn't making a radical statement and knows all the nuances.  Secondly. Literally anything can happen within a few bp.  Thirdly in this very narrow case I wouldn't stake much capital on this idea.  Mostly it will be random. 

However here is how I frame this. 

What is 100% certain if the fed hikes in September is the Fed funds rate will rise by 25bp (no they won't hike 50 you maniacs). At that point everything becomes less certain. The increased Fed funds rate will mechanically lift the entire curve but the shortest end of the curve is already roughly half way up because the hike is a coin flip.  Because of that every point in the curve is already mechanically pulled up by some amount.  

How much?   Well the 30 year mostly doesn't give any fucks at about the level of the fed funds rate from a mechanical sense.  The 10 year doesnt give maybe one or two fuck. So doesn't give a fuck.  The 2 year actually cares a little.  But not as much as you might think because it doesn't particularly care from a mechanical standpoint about whether a hike is in September or December. 

So mostly the mechanical rate hike influence is not important to the yield curve BUT if anything it is slightly higher yields in the front and decreasingly slightly higher yields for long maturities. 

So now you have to think about the "signal" of the rate hike.  That has three dimensions which are NOT orthogonal.  

1. Signal for future hikes
2. Signal for a policy mistake 
3. Some sort of "credibility signal

In terms of signal for future hikes often the first hike is followed by more hikes (a hiking cycle is kicked off).   If this hike is one of those the upward pressure on yields would likely be bigger and across the entire curve again with decreasing impact as maturity point is chosen. BUT This isn't one of those.  There is NO reason for markets to believe a hiking cycle has commenced

Will the market see this as a policy mistake (shouldn't have hiked at all!).  Maybe.  If so the reaction will be a downward pressure on yields offsetting the mechanical upward pressure and probably pushing long term yields down because they give few fucks about the hike but care quite a bit about an uncalled for hike.  I strongly doubt that market participants will view the hike as a policy mistake.

As a credibility signal who the fuck knows.  Do we really think that Warsh is suddenly going to be thought of as a credible inflation fighter because he was essentially dragged into a hike.  Maybe.  If so yields probably fall a bit on "credibility". 

Bottom line is we are talking handful (like 3-5bp) of 10 year yield moves cuz this isn't a beginning of a hiking cycle nor is it a policy mistake.

tweets.text:
History rarely repeats, but it certainly rhymes

I'm predicting an RWA cycle pattern similar to how the AI Agent boom played out in late 2024

The Agent timeline IIRC:

- July 2024: Truth Terminal + GOAT on Solana
- October 2024: Virtuals on Base 
- November 2024: Backrooms with FARTCOIN, Ai16z + several other behemoths emerged on Solana
- December 2024: AIXBT + Virtuals hit escape velocity in December
- January 2025: Top of cycle + peak euphoria

RWAs, and specifically tokenized stocks, exploded on Robinhood chain in July with a set list of 216 assets

But there's a broader offering within other ecosystems through platforms like @xStocksFi which has 715 assets & ETFs on SOL... this feeds platforms like @LaunchOnSF which is sitting around $28m MC

I'd bet that we are still in the early innings of how RWAs take off, which means it's likely there will be some large runners on Solana/ Base (maybe BNB or other) that drive attention to the leading "Pons" equivalents on those other chains

It's clear @base are placing bets on this narrative as they become more vocal about supporting high quality projects to keep up with Vlad's impeccable public bout with the AMC CEO y'day

Aerodrome is providing the LPs as 6 new stock tokens were added on Base yesterday; but the application layer for meme/stock launches is up for grabs

I've noticed @bankrbot acting quickly to additional assets but @Stonks_Exchange seems to becoming a viable challenger with a much lower $2m MC (runs the same model as Pons + STONK with buybacks, so success broadly driven by adoption)

IMO this gets really interesting when we get tokenized private equity assets + more penny stock tokens... the former offers more liquid valuations on otherwise illiquid assets and lowers the barrier to entry for normies to access exclusive offerings

Who are the other contenders we should be paying attention to?

Our echo chamber bubble is still too small for most equity analysts to realise that the economic activity is yet to be priced in on HOOD 

 Maybe AMC, Jinquan or the “Board Sit” movement has just peeped their radars

There’s a huge opportunity here for being early; lock in

Now that $MU to $SNDK have pulled a major recovery. 

Good to have a reminder that the memory bottleneck hasn’t changed!

Same with CW lasers… substrates… or others.

But short term sentiment (depending on prices/macro) often does.

I think a lot of demand imbalances get worse than people expect:

- There’s some Japanese distributors in Nikkei today saying memory demand deficit has reached 40-60% (67-150% higher than supply). With general prices going up 50% by years end.

- $SPCX isn’t included in the $1.3T hyperscaler capex figures (I think Wells Fargo ets. ~$263b AI capex), so total capex figures might be surprising.

- $SNDK expects 80% gross margins to continue into 2030… (welcome to S&P 100)

- and once again you have long term visibility into 2031 now with companies like Samsung

Memory is very really volatile… some of my positions are up 270%+, so I find it a bit easier to hold through volatile periods.

But regardless, operating fundamentals doesn’t always align with short term price movements.

Same concept can be applied to other sectors.
